Situation1: They maintain daily communication with their parents, sharing detailed updates and responding promptly to messages.
Expectation2: Listen actively and provide emotional support when needed.
Situation2: Your friend calls, sounding very upset, and asks if you have a moment to talk about a recent argument with their partner.
Story: My phone buzzed just as I was about to call my mom, like I do every evening. It was Mia, my best friend, her name flashing urgently on the screen. I answered, and her voice trembled as she told me about a huge fight with her boyfriend. She needed me—someone to listen, to help her sort through the mess of her feelings. I glanced at the clock. My parents would be waiting for my call, expecting to hear about my day, to know I was safe and well. They always worried if I was late, and I knew my mom would start texting soon, asking if everything was okay. I wanted to be there for Mia, to give her my full attention, but I also didn’t want to let my parents down or make them anxious. My heart pounded as I tried to figure out how to be a good friend and a good daughter at the same time, feeling the weight of both expectations pressing in on me.
